findings.description: The module docstring on line 7 contains a corrupted URL: `http�localhost:8901` where `://` was replaced by a single replacement character. This was likely introduced during the fix round when changing the port from 8795 to 8901. Should be `http://localhost:8901`.

The `current_tab()` function (lines 138-150) was changed from checking `ENGINE.name == "chrome-cdp"` to duck-typing with `hasattr(ENGINE, "_targets")` and `hasattr(ENGINE, "base") and hasattr(ENGINE, "user")`. While this avoids the AttributeError, it remains fragile: any engine with a `_targets` method will use the first branch, and any engine with `base`/`user` attributes will use the second, regardless of whether those attributes/APIs are compatible. The proper fix is a common interface (e.g., `engine.get_current_tab()`) on all engine classes. This is a sibling issue to the original `current_tab-camofox-path-fragile` finding that the fix round attempted to address but didn't fully resolve.

The watch server exposes /takeover, /release, /input, /start endpoints with no authentication (lines 230-258). This was an 'ask-user' finding in the previous round. Since watch/server.py was modified in the fix round but this issue was not addressed, it remains. Any process on localhost can control the browser, inject keystrokes/clicks, or start tasks. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 only (line 265), which mitigates but doesn't eliminate the risk (compromised local web app or malicious browser extension could hijack the agent). The threat model should be documented explicitly.

The fix round removed all `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` headers (previously on _send, do_OPTIONS, and /frame endpoints). This follows the original finding's recommendation to 'omit the header entirely for localhost-only services.' However, if chat_widget.html is ever served from a different origin (different port, file://, or another domain), it will break due to same-origin policy. The chat_widget.html currently hardcodes `const API = "http://127.0.0.1:8901";` and the watch server serves its own UI at `/`, so this may be intentional. Worth confirming this is the desired behavior.

testing_summary: Static analysis review only. No tests executed. The fix round addressed port-mismatch, hardcoded-path, cors-wildcard, inaccurate-dependency-free-claim, and partially addressed current_tab-camofox-path-fragile. The ask-user findings (world-writable-tmp-files, approval-file-race-condition, no-authentication-on-control-api, chrome-user-data-dir-in-tmp) remain in unchanged files.
risk_rationale: The fix round successfully resolved the critical bugs (port mismatch, hardcoded path) and the info-level CORS issue. One minor typo was introduced in the docstring. The current_tab() fragility was improved but not fully resolved. Remaining security issues are documented ask-user items requiring architectural decisions, not code defects. The change is well-bounded and safe to merge with the typo fixed.
